title: Should Gatekeepers Decide Which Local News You Get to See?
excerpt: Recent Rochdale Daily posts have remained pending approval in a major local Facebook group, prompting questions about moderation, free expression and the role of independent local journalism.
body:
Recent posts from Rochdale Daily submitted to the Rochdale Noticeboard Facebook group have remained pending approval rather than appearing publicly. The group is administered by several individuals, including Labour and Conservative councillors alongside other prominent local community figures. The reasons for those posts remaining pending are not publicly known, and there may be a number of explanations, from routine moderation to administrative delays or editorial decisions.

Nevertheless, it raises an important question about how independent journalism reaches local audiences.

As a newly established publication, Rochdale Daily has no affiliation with any political party. Our role is not to campaign for Labour, Reform UK, the Conservatives, the Liberal Democrats or any other political organisation. Our responsibility is to report local news accurately, fairly and in the public interest.

In recent months Reform UK has experienced growing electoral support nationally, something reflected in recent election results and opinion polling. Reporting that political reality should not be mistaken for endorsing it. Equally, reporting criticism of any political party should not automatically be interpreted as opposition to that party. Journalism exists to inform, not to campaign.

Independent publishers inevitably ask difficult questions. Sometimes those questions are uncomfortable for those in positions of authority. That is not a flaw in journalism; it is one of its core purposes.

Increasingly, public debate can become dominated by labels rather than evidence. Terms such as 'misinformation', 'divisive' or 'hate' are important where they accurately describe content, but they should never replace reasoned discussion. If reporting is inaccurate, those inaccuracies should be identified and corrected. If an article is defamatory, the offending statements should be clearly identified. If a factual claim is wrong, it should be rebutted with evidence.

The purpose of Rochdale Daily is straightforward: to publish lawful, evidence-based local journalism that reflects the issues local people are discussing. That includes stories which some readers will agree with and others will disagree with.

Whether recent moderation decisions affecting Rochdale Daily are connected to editorial policy, administrative workload or something else entirely is ultimately a matter for the group's administrators to explain. We make no allegation as to their motivation.

However, the broader principle remains. A healthy democracy depends upon robust debate, independent journalism and the free exchange of ideas within the law. Readers should have the opportunity to assess reporting for themselves and reach their own conclusions.

At Rochdale Daily, we will continue reporting local stories without fear or favour, regardless of which political party benefits or faces scrutiny.
